page.overview:
Who is Hisa?

Hisa grew up in a village in the Fire Nation. As a result of her experiences there, she developed a dislike of the police and a general distrust of others. At one point, two of her acquaintances died. She subsequently took in their orphaned children, Jian, Kibi, and Ming Ming; the three soon began to call her "Auntie". As the children's parents had always wished to raise them in the United Republic of Nations, Hisa moved to Republic City along with the three. In doing so, she was assisted by an old friend, Hai Jun, whom she wanted to stay with the small group.

Eventually, Hai Jun disappeared from his hotel in Republic City. Suspecting the reason for this, Hisa sought to protect her new family by forbidding Jian, Ming Ming, and Kibi from searching for their friend or contacting the Republic City Police. However, the children disobeyed and attempted to open a missing person case at the police headquarters. Hisa followed them and angrily stormed into the station, scolding them for their actions and trying to cut off their conversation with a local detective, Mako. When the latter asked her to stay and explain the situation, Hisa claimed that no one had gone missing. As she took the children away, Hisa warned Mako to leave them alone.

Later that day, Hisa went to Hai Jun's room at the Ember Sea Suites, where she found a note among his belongings. As she was reading it, Mako entered the apartment, and the two questioned each other about their presence there before fleeing. Mako gave chase, yelling that the paper was evidence and that he was trying to help her. In the pursuit, he attempted to grab the paper, ripping it in half. Despite losing half of the note, Hisa managed to escape.

After boarding a freight boat bound for Penquan Island, Hisa and the children encountered Mako in the sleeping quarters. She startled him and angrily asked whether he had followed them. Mako denied this, swearing that he did not know they would be on the ship. When she asked what he was doing there, he replied that it was the only way to Penquan Island he could find. She pressed him further, asking why he was going to Penquan Island, and he admitted that although he did not know what kind of trouble she or Hai Jun were in, he wanted to help. She asserted that she did not want his help. Bolin entered the conversation, pointing them to a pot of stew and introducing himself as Mako's brother. When Hisa left with the three children, Bolin remarked that she did not like Mako.
